blocks.instruction: Leia o texto e escolha a alternativa correta. Algumas perguntas pedem inferência — a resposta não está escrita com todas as letras.
blocks.passage:
Running an end-to-end logistics operation means seeing inbound, warehousing, transport and last mile as one single system. A late inbound truck at 8 a.m. becomes a missed picking slot at 11, a delayed outbound at 2, and an unhappy customer by dinner. Nothing is isolated — every hour touches the next.

Experienced logistics leaders watch three things every day: flow at each stage, exceptions, and customer impact. Is everything moving on the plan? Which shipments have drifted off script? And which of those drifts will actually matter to the people who paid for them?

The skill at this level is not perfection; it is honest, early attention. A problem caught at 9 a.m. is usually cheap to fix. The same problem at 4 p.m. is expensive for everyone.

items.q: According to the text, what does running an end-to-end operation mean?
options: Seeing every stage as one single system
items.why: "seeing inbound, warehousing, transport and last mile as one single system".

items.q: Which three things do experienced leaders watch every day?
items.why: "they watch three things every day: flow at each stage, exceptions, and customer impact".

items.q: What happens to a late inbound truck at 8 a.m., according to the text?
options: It only affects the inbound team
It is fixed automatically by the system
It ripples into missed picking, delayed outbound and an unhappy customer
items.why: O texto descreve a cadeia: janela de separação perdida às 11, saída atrasada às 2 e cliente insatisfeito no jantar.

items.q: Which statement would the author most likely DISAGREE with?
options: A delay in one stage can affect all the others
Every hour of the operation is connected to the next
Chasing perfection matters more than early attention
Catching a problem early is usually cheaper
items.why: Inferência: o texto diz que a habilidade "não é perfeição; é atenção honesta e precoce".

items.q: The line "A problem caught at 9 a.m. is cheap; at 4 p.m. it is expensive" suggests that…
options: Morning shifts are more skilled than afternoon shifts
Problems should be ignored until the afternoon
Most problems solve themselves during the day
Timing is central to controlling the cost of a problem
items.why: Inferência: o mesmo problema custa mais quanto mais tarde é tratado — o momento importa tanto quanto a solução.

blocks.instruction: Ouça James conduzindo o stand-up das 8:30. Responda sem ler a transcrição — ela só aparece depois de corrigir.

audio.text:
Right, quick stand-up, then we get moving. We have three inbound issues this morning, and I want us to act on them now, not at lunch.

First, the truck from the port is running ninety minutes late. That sounds small, but it means we lose the ten-thirty picking slot, and if we lose that slot, the afternoon outbound to the north region slips. So Sara, I want you to call the port and get a firm time, and meanwhile the team should start picking the orders we can already fulfil.

Second, one pallet came in damaged overnight. Right now it looks like it only affects two customer orders, so it is annoying but not a crisis. Log it, flag the two accounts, and move on.

Third — and this is the one that worries me — a supplier is sending the wrong reference again. If nobody catches it before eleven, it goes straight onto the wrong lorry and we spend all afternoon unpicking it. So please check the labels at goods-in before anything is loaded.

Remember, none of these is isolated. A slow morning here becomes an expensive evening downstairs. Catch it now while it is still cheap.
audio.label: Ouça quantas vezes precisar. A transcrição aparece depois de corrigir.

items.q: Why does James say the ninety-minute delay is not small?
options: It cancels the whole morning shift
It means losing the picking slot and slipping the afternoon outbound
It will upset the port authorities
items.why: "we lose the ten-thirty picking slot, and if we lose that slot, the afternoon outbound to the north region slips".

items.q: What does James ask Sara to do about the late truck?
options: Wait until lunch for an update
Call the port and get a firm time
Send another truck to the port
items.why: "Sara, I want you to call the port and get a firm time".

items.q: How does James treat the damaged pallet?
options: As a reason to stop all outbound
As the biggest problem of the day
As annoying but not a crisis — log it and move on
items.why: "it is annoying but not a crisis. Log it, flag the two accounts, and move on."

items.q: Why does the wrong supplier reference worry James most?
options: Because the supplier will cancel the contract
Because it costs more than the late truck
Because if it is not caught, it wastes the whole afternoon unpicking
Because it always damages the pallets
items.why: Inferência: se ninguém flagra antes das 11, vai na lorry errada e a tarde inteira é gasta desfazendo o erro.

items.q: What is James's main message to the team?
options: The evening team should handle everything
Perfection is the goal for the morning
Small issues connect, so catch them early while they are still cheap
Each issue is separate and can wait
items.why: Inferência: "none of these is isolated… Catch it now while it is still cheap" — atenção precoce evita custo alto.

blocks.instruction: O vocabulário da lição aparece aqui em frases novas. Escolha o sentido ou a palavra que cabe no contexto.

items.q: "We manage the whole chain end-to-end, from the port to the customer's door." End-to-end means…
options: covering the whole process from start to finish
items.why: End-to-end = de ponta a ponta: do início ao fim do processo.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "If the truck is late, we miss the ___ and the afternoon dispatch slips."
items.why: Picking slot = janela de separação; perdê-la atrasa a saída.

items.q: "Two shipments have drifted off the plan since this morning." To drift means to…
options: move slowly away from the plan
items.why: To drift = desviar, afastar-se aos poucos do previsto.

items.q: "A damaged pallet is a normal exception, not a disaster." An exception is…
options: a case that departs from the normal plan
items.why: Exception = exceção: um caso que foge do fluxo normal e precisa de resposta.

items.q: Choose the correct word: "Nothing here works in ___ — every stage affects the next."
items.why: "work in isolation" = trabalhar isolado; a lição insiste que nenhum estágio é isolado.

blocks.instruction: Expressões e phrasal verbs que aparecem no dia a dia de uma operação logística. Escolha o sentido no contexto.

items.q: "We need to catch the wrong label before eleven." To catch a problem means to…
options: notice and stop it in time
items.why: To catch = flagrar, perceber e deter a tempo.

items.q: "The port delay will ripple into the afternoon dispatch." This means it will…
options: spread and affect a later stage
items.why: Ripple into = repercutir, espalhar o efeito para uma etapa seguinte.

items.q: "Please flag the two affected accounts for the service team." To flag means to…
items.why: To flag = sinalizar, marcar algo para receber atenção.

items.q: "We agreed the fix but nobody followed through." They…
options: failed to carry it to completion
items.why: Follow through = levar até o fim o que foi combinado.

items.q: "Let's get moving before the picking slot closes." This means…
items.why: Get moving = começar a agir, colocar as coisas em andamento agora.
